ntp-saat-esitleme.title: Why is accurate time important in network diagnosis?
ntp-saat-esitleme.excerpt: If the clocks of different devices do not match, it becomes difficult to understand the sequence of a fault. Time synchronization is the basis for comparing logs and scan records.
ntp-saat-esitleme.body:
If the clocks of different devices do not match, it becomes difficult to understand the sequence of a fault. Time synchronization is the basis for comparing logs and scan records.

Basic approach

NTP is a protocol for clock synchronization over the network. Time zone display and the actual time accuracy of the system are different matters. If one log uses UTC and the other uses local time, the same event may appear to occur at different times.

Application steps

  1. Check the time source of client, server and network devices.
  2. Add time zone or UTC information to reports.
  3. Record the time difference at the time of the error and take this difference into account when comparing the logs.

Practical example

If the camera log shows 18:00 and the recording server log shows 21:00, check the time zones first. A three-hour display difference does not necessarily mean that there are three hours between actual events.

Interpret the result correctly

Changing the time suddenly may affect running applications. Follow central time policy in corporate environments. An accurate desktop clock does not prove that all devices are synchronized; The source and synchronization status should be checked separately.

Source and follow-up reading

Protocol or command details: RFC 5905. The steps and example scenario are IPScans editorial narrative.

acik-port-risk.title: I found open port: what should I check now?
acik-port-risk.excerpt: Open port is not a security vulnerability by itself. The question is whether the service is necessary, who has access to it, and how it is protected.
acik-port-risk.body:
Open port is not a security vulnerability by itself. The question is whether the service is necessary, who has access to it, and how it is protected.

Basic approach

Port scanning monitors reachability from a specific source location. A service that appears open on the local network may be closed on the internet; The opposite is also possible with different guidance and rules. It is not correct to convert open, closed and filtered statuses into the same risk score.

Application steps

  1. Identify the service owner and business need.
  2. Document access with source network, protocol, and authentication conditions.
  3. Shut down unnecessary service in a planned manner; Check the update and access policy of the required service.

Practical example

A print service may be expected to be reachable from its running VLAN. Accessing the same service from the guest network or the internet requires separate review depending on the design. The number of ports alone does not explain the magnitude of the risk.

Interpret the result correctly

The scan result does not guarantee the software version or the absence of vulnerabilities. Closing the port without recognizing the service may disrupt production. After the change, verify both the access limit and the operation of the legitimate application and prepare the rollback path.

Source and follow-up reading

tarama-kapsami-planlama.title: Coverage and measurement plan before network scanning
tarama-kapsami-planlama.excerpt: A good discovery study does not start with typing a large range into the address box. The result is more easily verified when the purpose, scope, and expected devices are defined in advance.
tarama-kapsami-planlama.body:
A good discovery study does not start with typing a large range into the address box. The result is more easily verified when the purpose, scope, and expected devices are defined in advance.

Basic approach

Inventory discovery, service access control, and physical topology verification are different goals. Each requires different data sources. Giving the scanner more targets does not automatically increase the accuracy of the information; may increase time and network load.

Application steps

  1. Specify the address ranges in your management authority and the sensitive devices to exclude.
  2. Record maintenance time, protocols used, and expected load.
  3. Select several known devices in the control group and verify that they are ultimately found when the discovery is complete.

Practical example

For an office inventory, it is more useful to verify the relevant /24 subnet first than to accidentally try the entire 10.0.0.0/8 domain. Saving the VPN and virtual adapters as separate scopes keeps the source of the results clear.

Interpret the result correctly

Do not automatically delete undetected devices; There is a possibility of sleep, filtering or opt-out. Clearly indicate areas that were not scanned in your report. The criterion for success is not only a quick finish but also producing verifiable results within the targeted scope.

Source and follow-up reading

tarayici-performans-karsilastirma.title: How do you compare IP scanners fairly?
tarayici-performans-karsilastirma.excerpt: The fastest scanner claim is not meaningful unless tools doing the same job are measured under the same conditions. Depth of discovery and accuracy should be compared as well as the number of devices.
tarayici-performans-karsilastirma.body:
The fastest scanner claim is not meaningful unless tools doing the same job are measured under the same conditions. Depth of discovery and accuracy should be compared as well as the number of devices.

Basic approach

The total time of a tool that only pings and a tool that collects identity and service information is not directly comparable. Pre-full cache, timeout, parallelism and network conditions affect the result. Writing the scope of the test makes the comparison repeatable.

Application steps

  1. Use the same target range and common protocol scope.
  2. Separate cold and hot cache conditions and do multiple iterations.
  3. Report time, number of known devices found, misclassification, processor and memory usage.

Practical example

If one tool finds 20 real devices in 2 seconds and the other finds 30 real devices in 4 seconds, considering the first one as superior based on the time alone is an underestimation. You also can't measure missed devices without the expected 30-device checklist.

Interpret the result correctly

Synthetic testing and loopback testing are not substitutes for a real device fleet. Express results limited to the tested environment. Share numbers with hardware, version and method used, rather than unquantified world leadership claims.

Source and follow-up reading

Protocol or command details: RFC 2330. The steps and example scenario are IPScans editorial narrative.

ag-bakim-kontrol-listesi.title: Monthly network maintenance checklist for small office
ag-bakim-kontrol-listesi.excerpt: The purpose of regular maintenance is not to change all the settings every month. Small, verifiable checks are needed to see that inventory, access, and backups are still as expected.
ag-bakim-kontrol-listesi.body:
The purpose of regular maintenance is not to change all the settings every month. Small, verifiable checks are needed to see that inventory, access, and backups are still as expected.

Basic approach

An initial inventory should include device ID, address, responsible person, and last verification time. Comparing network changes to this record makes it easier to spot new devices, lost services, and old names. If the inventory does not have a date, its currentness cannot be evaluated.

Application steps

  1. Get new discovery in managed scope and review device changes with previous record.
  2. Compare DHCP reservations, DNS names, and required administrative access.
  3. Verify that the configuration backup exists and the restore procedure is known.

Practical example

If a new printer appears at the end of the month, don't just add its IP; Record its location, principal, and address allocation method. If the old printer is not visible, ask if it has been moved or turned off before deregistering it.

Interpret the result correctly

Schedule updates according to manufacturer notes; Do not reboot all devices at the same time. Adapt the checklist to the actual needs of your small office. DHCP registration or a single scan result does not prove that the device has been working for the entire month.

Source and follow-up reading

Protocol or command details: RFC 2131. The steps and example scenario are IPScans editorial narrative.

ip-adresi-nedir.title: What Is an IP Address and How Does It Work?
ip-adresi-nedir.excerpt: The basics of IP addresses, the difference between IPv4 and IPv6, and how the internet handles addressing.
ip-adresi-nedir.body:
An IP address identifies a network interface within an addressing scope. A device may have several addresses, and private addresses can be reused across separate networks. Think of it like the address on an envelope — it's how data packets know where to go.

What's the difference between IPv4 and IPv6?

IPv4 addresses are 32 bits long, written as four segments like 192.168.1.1. The total address space is about 4.3 billion; scarcity of public allocations has encouraged extensive use of NAT. IPv6 is 128 bits long, written like 2001:0db8:85a3::8a2e:0370:7334, and offers a practically inexhaustible address space.

Public vs. private IP

  • Public IP: The address your ISP assigns you that's visible on the internet.
  • Private IP: The address your router hands out to distinguish devices on your home or office network (e.g. 192.168.x.x).

When you connect to a website, your browser resolves the destination server's IP via DNS, then data packets travel back and forth over that address. Want to check your own? Try our IP lookup tool.

Why does your IP matter?

It can reveal your approximate location, ISP, and sometimes your organization — which is why privacy-conscious users increasingly rely on VPNs.

internet-hizini-artirma.title: 7 Ways to Improve Your Internet Speed
internet-hizini-artirma.excerpt: Practical tips to fix slow internet: router placement, DNS settings and more.
internet-hizini-artirma.body:
Slow internet can stem from many different factors. The seven steps below make a noticeable difference in most home and office networks.

  1. Place your router correctly: a central, open, elevated spot reduces signal loss.
  2. Use the 5 GHz band: faster than 2.4 GHz, though with slightly shorter range.
  3. Switch your DNS: 1.1.1.1 (Cloudflare) or 8.8.8.8 (Google) can be compared with your current resolver. Changing DNS does not directly increase download bandwidth and can affect internal name resolution.
  4. Disable background traffic: automatic updates and cloud sync quietly eat bandwidth.
  5. Prefer a wired connection: Ethernet delivers stability Wi-Fi often can't match.
  6. Keep your router's firmware current: vendor updates include performance and security fixes.
  7. Test regularly: use our speed test tool to confirm you're actually getting the speed you're paying for.

When should you call your ISP?

If tests stay significantly below the promised speed even over a wired connection, record the device, link speed, time and background traffic before contacting your ISP. This result alone does not locate the fault.

vpn-nedir.title: What Is a VPN, How Does It Work, and Do You Really Need One?
vpn-nedir.excerpt: A clear look at how VPNs encrypt your traffic, how they affect your privacy, and when they actually help.
vpn-nedir.body:
A VPN (Virtual Private Network) creates an encrypted "tunnel" between your device and a VPN server. Inside that tunnel, your ISP and anyone else on the same network can't see the contents of your traffic.

What happens to your IP when you use a VPN?

You appear to browse the internet from the VPN server's IP address. Sites you visit see the VPN provider's IP, not your real one. You can verify this yourself with our IP lookup tool — check before and after connecting.

What a VPN fixes — and what it doesn't

  • Can help: protect traffic routed through the tunnel from local observers and provide remote access. Split tunneling, DNS configuration and provider policies affect coverage; anonymity is not guaranteed.
  • Doesn't fix: being identified through logged-in accounts, browser fingerprinting, or malware.

How to choose a VPN

Be cautious of "no-logs" claims that aren't backed by an independent audit. Some free VPNs fund themselves by selling user data — which defeats the whole purpose.

yaygin-port-numaralari-rehberi.title: A Guide to Common Port Numbers: Frequently Used Services
yaygin-port-numaralari-rehberi.excerpt: 80, 443, 22, 3389... what do these port numbers actually mean? A network and security primer.
yaygin-port-numaralari-rehberi.body:
A port is like a numbered doorway that routes traffic to a specific service running on a server. The IP address gets you to the right device; the port number gets you to the right application on it.

The most common ports

  • 20/21 — FTP: file transfer protocol.
  • 22 — SSH: secure remote access to servers.
  • 25 — SMTP: sending email.
  • 53 — DNS: domain name resolution.
  • 80 — HTTP: unencrypted web traffic.
  • 110 — POP3 / 143 — IMAP: email retrieval protocols.
  • 443 — HTTPS: encrypted web traffic — the modern standard.
  • 3306 — MySQL: database connections.
  • 3389 — RDP: Windows remote desktop.
  • 8080 — HTTP-alt: commonly used in dev environments or proxies.

When is an open port a risk?

An open port alone isn't a vulnerability — but unnecessarily exposed management ports (like 3389 or 22) are a top target for attackers. Use our port check tool to quickly see what's exposed on a host.

A practical tip

Keep management ports behind a VPN where possible, enforce strong authentication, and shut down services you're not using.
